**Policy type**  
- You have a **Third‑Party bike insurance policy** (Third‑Party liability) – the basic, mandatory vehicle insurance required for bike owners in India.

**What it covers**  
- **Third‑party liability** – it pays for financial or legal losses you cause to:  
  • Any third‑party person (coverage is **unlimited**), and  
  • Third‑party property (coverage up to **Rs. 1 Lac**).  

- The policy is valid for **one year** (Policy Starts: June 2026, expires June 2027).  

**What it does not cover**  
- Damage to your own bike (repair costs are not paid).  
- Use of the vehicle for hire or reward, carriage of goods (other than samples or personal luggage), organized racing, pacemaking, speed testing, reliability trials, or any purpose connected with motor trade.  

These are the only coverage details provided in the document.

raw_output_redacted:
**Type of policy**  
- You have a **Third‑Party bike insurance policy (Third‑Party liability)** – the basic, mandatory vehicle insurance required for bike owners in India.  

**What it covers**  
- **Third‑party liability** – it pays for financial or legal losses you cause to:  
  * Any third‑party person (unlimited amount)  
  * Third‑party property (up to **Rs. 1 Lac**)  

- The policy **does not cover** damage to your own bike, theft, fire, calamities, rat‑bite damage, wear‑and‑tear, or tyre/tube replacement unless those items are damaged in an accident (in which case a 50 % depreciation applies).  

- **Use limitations** – the coverage is valid only when the bike is not used for: hire or reward, carriage of goods (other than samples or personal luggage), organized racing, pacemaking, speed testing, reliability trials, or any purpose connected with motor trade.  

- **Non‑OEM parts** – if you install non‑OEM parts (e.g., halogen bulbs, stereos, bifuel kits), you must inform the insurer so they can be added to the coverage.  

So, your policy is a mandatory third‑party liability bike insurance that protects third parties against injury or property loss caused by your bike, but it does **not** pay for repairs or loss of your own vehicle.

**Claim Process (as outlined by ACKO)**  

1. **Inform ACKO first** – Notify the insurer as soon as possible. You can do this through the ACKO website (acko.com) or, more quickly, via the **ACKO mobile app**.  

2. **Submit the required documents** – After you have reported the incident, you will be asked to upload the relevant paperwork (e.g., FIR/police report, proof of ownership, photos, etc.) through the app or the online portal.  

3. **Track the claim** – Once the claim is lodged, you can **track the real‑time status of your repair/claim** on the ACKO app.  

4. **Settlement** – If the claim is approved, ACKO will settle the approved claim amount as per the policy terms.  

---

**Important note for your current policy**

- Your policy (Policy No. **DBTR10541714586/01**) is a **Third‑Party Bike Insurance** plan.  
- This plan **covers only third‑party liabilities** and **does not pay for damage to your own bike**, including loss or theft.  

Therefore, a theft claim under this third‑party policy would **not be covered** and would be rejected. If you need coverage for theft or damage to your own bike, you would have to purchase a comprehensive (own‑damage) plan.

raw_output_redacted:
**Claim process if your bike is stolen**

1. **Inform ACKO immediately** – you can do this through the ACKO app or by visiting [acko.com](https://acko.com).  
2. **Submit the required claim details and documents** (police FIR, proof of ownership, etc.) through the app or the online portal.  
3. **Track the claim in real‑time** on the ACKO app until a decision is made and any approved amount is settled.

**Important note about coverage**

Your current policy is a **Third‑Party Only plan**. Under the “What’s not covered” section, theft of the vehicle is listed as a loss that is **not covered** by this policy. Therefore, a claim for a stolen bike is likely to be **rejected** because theft is not included in the coverage.  

If you need a policy that covers theft, you would have to upgrade to a comprehensive plan that includes that benefit.
final_answer_redacted:
**Claim process if your bike is stolen**

1. **Inform ACKO immediately** – you can do this through the ACKO app or by visiting [acko.com](https://acko.com).  
2. **Submit the required claim details and documents** (police FIR, proof of ownership, etc.) through the app or the online portal.  
3. **Track the claim in real‑time** on the ACKO app until a decision is made and any approved amount is settled.

**Important note about coverage**

Your current policy is a **Third‑Party Only plan**. Under the “What’s not covered” section, theft of the vehicle is listed as a loss that is **not covered** by this policy. Therefore, a claim for a stolen bike is likely to be **rejected** because theft is not included in the coverage.  

If you need a policy that covers theft, you would have to upgrade to a comprehensive plan that includes that benefit.
